steps.what: Read the placement brief before supervising students
inputs: placement brief already on the student record
outputs: what this visit needs to cover

steps.what: Supervise students' fieldwork, internship, and research in person
inputs: what this visit needs to cover
outputs: what she and the student agreed in the visit

tasks.design: She reads the placement brief in {DOCS} and supervises the student's fieldwork, internship, and research in person. The visit is not shortened. No machine files a supervision note, because a resident dossier write is not established as work she already does today.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is a conversation on site. A note in a resident record is not shown as a filing she already does after each visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the visit. A filing saving waits until someone confirms she already writes that note into the student record.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether the fieldwork is on track, and saying the right thing while she is there.
tasks.human_edge: She sees the student's research as it is happening and decides what to press on.
tasks.altitude: The week of fieldwork visits stays. She gains no new decision right, and no note is auto-filed.

reach.task: Confirm what the host saw on the same fieldwork
reach.learn: What the host saw that the student did not say

evidence.claim: Sitting with a student during fieldwork, an internship, or research is spoken work. The digest does not show a resident supervision note as a filing this task already does, so no file step is counted.

assumptions: Talking with the student or an in-house colleague is write_internal. A message to a host organisation outside the institution is not given a send step, because that message is not established as part of every visit.
The placement brief is already on the student record. She does not re-key the student id.
No system runs, so upkeep is zero. A plain save of a visit note is not gated and is not counted as time saved.
unknowns: After a visit, does she write a supervision note into the student record, and how many minutes does that keying take?
research_questions: On one programme, what share of supervision time is typing a note that another person later relies on, as against the visit itself?

incremental.description: No system runs on the visit, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of site visits. The reading and the supervision stay as they are. A supervision note is not counted, because a resident filing is not shown as work she already does.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Grade class work, assignments, and papers

steps.what: Read students' class work, assignments, and papers
inputs: the submission already open on the course

steps.what: Evaluate the work and state each grade herself
Draft a rubric comment from the quoted passage and her grade
outputs: a draft comment tied to that passage

loop.input: The grade she stated, the rubric item she selected, and the passage she quoted from the open paper.
loop.output: A short comment that cites that passage and does not change her grade.
loop.check: The passage is in the paper, and the comment does not propose a different grade.
loop.stop: The rubric item has no quoted passage, or after one redraft. She then writes that comment while checking.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed rule can check length and citation form, but the comment has to follow the passage she quoted.

steps.what: Check the comment matches the quoted passage and accept her grade
inputs: a draft comment tied to that passage

steps.what: Publish the accepted grade into the student record
outputs: the grade stored on the course record and the student record

steps.what: Tell the student the result in the room when they ask
outputs: what she explained to the student

tasks.design: She reads the paper in {DOCS} and states every grade herself. A bounded loop on the {LMS} drafts a rubric comment only from the passage she quoted and the grade she stated. She checks that the comment matches that passage. A separate records write then publishes only the accepted grade into the course record and the student record. That second entry is filing she already does. The model does not choose the grade. Telling the student in the room stays hers.
tasks.previous_blocker: The grade is a judgement on an open paper, and the same result is keyed again into the student record by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: The second entry is a fixed write of a grade she has already stated, and a short comment can be drafted from a passage she quoted.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding what the paper deserves. Long essays often have no clean passage for a rubric item.
tasks.human_edge: She sets the result. A draft comment does not.
tasks.altitude: The week of reading and grading stays, and she still sets every result. Only the second keying of an accepted grade, and the first typing of a comment that has a quoted passage, leave her desk.

reach.task: Double-mark a sample of the same papers
reach.learn: Where two examiners read one rubric item differently

evidence.claim: A learning-system feature drafts text and rubric feedback from the instructor's notes. The marker still edits it.

In a 2026 Michigan economics trial, assistants edited rubric suggestions on 1,366 essays from 354 students and agreed with 88 percent of the model's judgments. Revisions were better. The study reports no time data, so the 88 percent is not used as a time saving.
At Radboud, grades entered in Brightspace must also be published in OSIRIS. That is a second entry of the same grade, with no model.
Annex III point 3 lists admission, evaluating learning outcomes, setting an education level, and detecting cheating in tests as high-risk uses.
Duties for AI grading and proctoring apply from 2 December 2027.
A grade set solely by a model is likely an article 22 decision, and systematic automated evaluation needs a data-protection impact assessment.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results. Only the board sanctions fraud.
Works-council consent is required for a system able to monitor staff, such as a view of each examiner's marking.

assumptions: The student id and the course id come from the submission already open in the {LMS}. She does not re-key them.

The grade is the scale point she states while evaluating. The model never chooses or changes it. The rubric item is the criterion she selects. The quoted passage is text she highlights in the open paper.

The draft may only comment on that passage and that grade. If the passage is missing, the loop stops and she writes the comment in the check. That writing stays inside the check and is not counted again as extra hours.

She accepts the grade in the check before the publish. The publish writes that accepted grade, and the comment she accepted, into the course record and the student record. It is the second entry she already makes, not a save of a scratch note. She does not also key the same grade by hand.

Because she states and accepts every grade, the record write is not a decision made solely by a model. A data-protection assessment and a student notice are still in the build, because student papers are processed. Comment drafting is treated as in scope for the later grading duties until counsel says otherwise. This is not a proctoring system and it does not infer emotion.

The draft is not used to time or score her. No per-examiner marking view is built. A second examiner double-marks a sample; that time is the other role. About one hour per 100 of her grading hours is her re-read when that sample disagrees, plus the rare grade she keys herself if the record write fails.
Telling a student in the room is write_internal. Closed questions are not auto-marked here, because the task is class work, assignments, and papers, and a paper is not a closed item.
The prior that a model does most of this task is not followed. She keeps the grade decision.
unknowns: How many minutes is the second entry of one grade, and what share of her items are essays with no passage she can quote?
research_questions: On one course, what share of grading time is the second entry into the student record, measured apart from reading the paper?

incremental.description: A second examiner double-marks a sample of the same papers.
She re-reads papers the sample sends back, and keys a grade herself if the record write fails.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A batch of open papers where she has stated every grade. The publish is the second entry of that grade into the student record. The low end is a week of long essays where most rubric items have no clean passage, so the comment draft stops and only the grade entry remains. An 88 percent agreement figure from one study is not used as a time saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read topics in children's literature, learning, development, and reading instruction
Prepare what this lecture will cover for these students
outputs: the outcomes and examples she will use

steps.what: Draft lecture notes only from the outcomes she prepared
inputs: the outcomes and examples she will use

loop.input: The outcomes and examples she listed for this lecture.
loop.output: Lecture notes that use only those outcomes and examples.
loop.check: Every claim in the notes is one she listed.
loop.stop: A claim is not in her list, or after one redraft. She writes that part while checking.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed outline can set the headings, but the sentences have to follow the outcomes she chose.

steps.what: Check every claim she will say in the lectures
outputs: the notes she will speak from

steps.what: Deliver the lectures to undergraduate or graduate students
inputs: the notes she will speak from

tasks.design: She reads the topic and prepares the outcomes herself. A bounded loop drafts notes in {DOCS} from that list only. She checks every claim she will actually say, then delivers the lecture to the students. The lecture is not shortened. The notes are not filed by a second step, and a private draft is not gated, because a course-page posting is not shown as work she already does on every lecture.
tasks.previous_blocker: The lecture is spoken in the room, and the notes have to match what she is willing to say.
tasks.enabler_now: A first draft can be typed from outcomes she has already listed, and she still checks every claim.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what is true enough to say, and teaching it to the room.
tasks.human_edge: She decides the content and delivers the lecture. The draft does not speak.
tasks.altitude: The lecture week stays. She still chooses the content and delivers it. A first draft of notes is the only change, and she still checks it.

reach.task: Hold the programme outcomes this lecture must cover
reach.learn: Which outcomes this session is supposed to serve

evidence.claim: Annex III point 3 lists admission, evaluating learning outcomes, setting an education level, and detecting cheating in tests as high-risk uses.

Typing a first draft of lecture notes from outcomes she already listed can be checked by her. Delivering the lecture is spoken work and is not shortened. No time figure is taken from the grading studies.

assumptions: The outcomes and examples are the list she states before the draft. The draft adds no claim outside that list. No student personal data is in the notes.
Delivering the lecture is write_internal. It is not a send outside the organisation.
A refused claim is rewritten inside the check, which stays at full remaining time, so upkeep beyond that check is zero.
Posting the notes on the course page is not counted. The digest shows a second entry for grades, not for lecture notes.
The notes are not used to score her teaching.
unknowns: What share of her lecture preparation is typing notes, as against choosing examples, and how often she discards a draft?
research_questions: On one course, how many minutes of note typing remain after she checks a draft built only from outcomes she listed?

incremental.description: Rewrites of a refused claim sit inside the check, so no extra upkeep is added.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of lectures where she has already listed the outcomes, including sessions on children's literature and reading instruction. The draft types notes from that list and she still checks every claim. The low end is a week where she rewrites most of the draft while checking. The lecture itself is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the aim of the coming classroom discussions
inputs: the session aim already on the course

steps.what: Initiate, facilitate, and moderate classroom discussions
Choose the next speaker and close the classroom discussion

tasks.design: She reads the aim, then initiates, facilitates, and moderates the classroom discussion in the room. The discussion is not recorded and is not filed. A plain save of a private jotting is not added and is not gated.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is a live conversation. Who speaks next depends on the room.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the discussion. A filing saving waits until someone confirms she already writes a record another person relies on.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the room and keeping the discussion on the point without taking it over.
tasks.human_edge: She hears who is lost and chooses the next speaker in the moment.
tasks.altitude: The discussion stays hers. Nothing in the week moves to a machine.

reach.task: Listen for questions the room did not settle
reach.learn: Which points students still want taken up next time

evidence.claim: Moderating a live classroom discussion is spoken work in the room. A discussion note is not shown as a resident filing this task already does, so no file step is counted.

assumptions: Moderating the discussion is write_internal, not a read and not a send outside the institution.
No system runs, so upkeep is zero. The discussion is not recorded and is not used to score her.
Documents are a small share of this task. They are not treated as a filing another person relies on.
unknowns: After a discussion, does she write anything that another person later relies on, and how long does that take?
research_questions: On one course, is any record of the discussion read by someone other than the teacher who led it?

incremental.description: No system runs on the discussion, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of classroom discussions. Starting, running, and closing them stay in the room. A discussion note is not counted, because a resident filing is not shown as work she already does.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week of fieldwork, grading judgement, lectures, and classroom discussions stays with her. She still sets every grade. Only the second keying of an accepted grade, the first typing of a comment that quotes the paper, and a first draft of lecture notes she still checks, leave her desk.
reach: A placement supervisor can confirm what the host saw on the same fieldwork.
A teaching assistant can double-mark a sample of papers.
An instructional coordinator can hold the programme outcomes a lecture must cover.
skills_to_grow: State the grade before any comment is drafted, and reject a comment that does not quote the paper.
Keep a lecture claim inside the outcomes she chose.
Leave a live discussion in the room rather than turning it into a file.
role.ambitious_version: The accepted grade reaches the course record and the student record in one write, and she still sets every result. Lectures and discussions stay spoken by her.
